newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Yachting: Peter Campbell's Rhumbline Column.

text.p: By Peter Campbell*
SYDNEY'S SUNMMER OF SAIL STARTS SATURDAY

Sydney's summer spectacle of sail begins on Saturday with the invitation race for the Telstra Cup offshore regatta, an eight-race series starting next Tuesday, and culminates in the Boxing Day start to the Telstra 52nd Sydney-Hobart.
The Telstra Cup promises to be one of the world's best regattas, boasting a state-of-the-art fleet of 50 IMS-designed racer and cruiser/racer yachts.

The Telstra Cup is a stand-alone regatta and while it has attracted most of the competitive yachts contesting the Sydney-Hobart, there are also interesting entries from several grand prix racers which are not sailing to Hobart.

One is Bashfull, the new and successful Sydney 36 designed by IAIN MURRAY and being strongly campaigned by API chief executive DAVID FULLER and property developer HUGO VAN KRETSCHMAR. After the Telstra Cup, Bashfull will be road transported to Melbourne for the Hewlett Packard Port Phillip Regatta in early January.

Another one to watch is Sea, the Mumm 36 now owned by advertising man and champion Sydney-Hobart helmsman STEVE KULMAR who is preparing for an Admiral's Cup campaign in England next July. Sea will also contest the Strathfield Car Radios Pittwater to Coffs Harbour race in a fleet of just over 80 boats.
AMERICAN SKIPPER FLIES IN FOR REGATTA

American Dr JIM HUNT has flown out from the U.S. West Coast specially to contest the Telstra Cup in his newly launched Mount Gay 30, My Tribe. HUNT arrived down at the Cruising Yacht Club of Australia on Thursday after a long flight across the Pacific to see his boat sitting in a pride of place in the pond in front of the clubhouse.

Designed by SCOTT JUTSON to the box rules of the Mount Gay (formerly Whitbread 30) international class, My Tribe is a sistership to the successful Razors Edge being campaigned by bluewater champion yachtsman and marketing man RAY STONE.
Razors Edge and My Tribe will be sailing under PHS rules, which allows the use of asymmetric spinnakers, in the Telstra Cup, but Razors Edge will contest the Hobart competing as an IMS entrant.
Six of the Telstra Cup races will be sailed offshore but next Tuesday two races will be sailed on Sydney Harbour in what will be a spectacular event as the big fleet charges up and down the harbour.

Among those to watch as GEORGE SNOW's Brindabella, WARWICK MILLER's Exile, the 80-footer Morning Glory owned by HASSO PLATTNER, the German industrialist and founder of the SAP computer company, and the about-to-be-launched IAIN MURRAY designed 60-footer Sydney, owned by CHARLES CURRAN, chairman of Capital Investments.

Sydney, built by Bashford International, the Nowra-based company in which MURRAY and CURRAN have each bought a major interest, will go in the water on Sunday to race in the Telstra Cup on Tuesday, with Murray at the helm.
EXILE IN TWILIGHT RACE COLLISION

International watch marketing guru WARWICK MILLER received a setback to his campaign for the Telstra Cup and Canon Big Boat Challenge (next Friday, December 20) when his Hong Kong-registered Exile was involved in a costly collision at the start of last Wednesday's CYCA twilight race on the harbour.

The 66-footer Exile, packed with crew and guests, was lining up for the start on right-of-way starboard tack when a heavy cruiser/racer reportedly came charging down the line on port tack and slammed into Exile's port topsides.

The pulpit, stanchions and safety lines were ripped off, the hull suffered two holes but the worst and most costly damage was to the primary coffee grinder as the bow of the other boat rode up over Exile's gunwale.

Exile will miss Saturday's Telstra Cup invitation race as crew and shipwrights repair the damage, said to run into tens of thousands of dollars, while a replacement coffee grinder is flown out from England.
MILLER hopes that temporary repairs can be made to the coffee grinder in time for the regatta and that a new one will be in Sydney in time for the Hobart race.
YACHTSMAN OF THE YEAR AWARD TO OLYMPIANS

It was full house at the Royal Sydney Yacht Squadron on Monday for the Australian Yachting Awards luncheon, with than 200 sailors and supporters packing the dining room for this prestigious annual award.
At A$80 a head, plus some spirited auctioning of yachting memorabillia, the luncheon was also an importing fund-raiser for the New South Wales Yachting Foundation.

As we suggested last week, the top award went to MITCH BOOTH and ANDREW LANDENBERGER, who won the silver medal in the Tornado catamaran class at the Atlanta Olympics. Booth also won the bronze in the same class at Barcelona and is already looking for gold at Sydney 2000.

However, in their campaign for the Sydney Olympics, BOOTH and LANDENBERGER have decided to run a two-boat programme, each skippering his own Tornado with a new crew in an intensive plan of racing in Australia and overseas.

The Youth Award went to another catamaran sailor, 18-year-old GLEN ASHBY from Bendigo, Victoria. ASHBY won the International A-class catamaran world championship for this single-handed cat in Spain this year, winning four of five races.
RICH PURSE FOR AUSTRALIA CUP

The world's richest prize purse in yachting, potentially more than A$350,00 has just been announced by the Royal Perth Yacht Club for its Australia Cup match racing series to be sailed on Matilda Bay, Perth, from February 3-9.
The bonus purse of A$350,000 is in addition to normal prizemoney for the regatta and will be awarded to the winner of the Cup if he can claim victory without losing a match.

Most of the world's top match racing sailors have been nominated for the event include Australia's PETER GILMOUR who won the Cup in 1987, 1989 and 1996. Other Australian skippers nominated are NEVILLE WITTEY who finished a close third in this year's event and DAVE CLARK who recently won the Lexcen Challenge and Australian match racing championship.

Other international sailors competing include former winner CHRIS LAW (Britain), BERTRAND PACE (France), MAGNUS HOLMBERG (Sweden), THIERRY PEPONNET (France), STEN MOHR (Denmark), ROY HEINER (Netherlands), GAVIN BRADY (New Zealand), MORGAN LARSON (United States) and SEBASTIEN DESTREMAU (Austria).
* Peter Campbell is the editor of Offshore Yachting magazine.
